issues.t: PowerShift automatic shudders and jerks from a stop
issues.sym: The car shudders, jerks or hesitates when pulling away or creeping in traffic, sometimes followed by a hard shift you feel through the steering wheel. It often gets worse over time.
issues.why: The PowerShift automatic is really two computer-controlled dry clutches, like a manual gearbox that shifts itself. The clutches wear and grab unevenly, which causes the shudder. This was the most-reported Fiesta problem and led to a class action and Ford warranty extensions.
issues.next: Have a Ford dealer check the clutches, seals and software. Ask with your VIN whether any extended clutch coverage still applies; most of it has run out by now, but some cars may still qualify.

issues.t: Transmission control module failure
issues.sym: A wrench or transmission warning light, the car refusing to start or go into gear, or the car suddenly dropping into neutral and losing power while driving.
issues.why: The computer that runs the PowerShift clutches sits on the transmission and can fail from heat and moisture. Ford issued several reprogramming bulletins and extended coverage on this module to 10 years or 150,000 miles on many cars.
issues.next: Losing drive in traffic is dangerous, so get it checked promptly. Have a dealer read the transmission codes and check your VIN for the extended module coverage.

issues.t: Automatic transmission fails and needs replacing
issues.sym: Slipping, banging into gear, losing power or the car not moving at all, often after earlier shudder repairs did not last.
issues.why: On the worst years the clutch packs, shift parts and control module can wear out together, and some owners end up needing a full transmission replacement.
issues.next: Get a written diagnosis before agreeing to a full replacement, and ask Ford about any goodwill help if the car has a history of transmission repairs.

issues.t: Transmission seal leak soaks the clutches
issues.sym: Oil drips from where the engine and transmission meet, and the car starts shuddering from a stop.
issues.why: The input shaft seals inside the PowerShift can leak gearbox oil onto the dry clutches. Ford issued a bulletin for fluid leaks combined with clutch shudder.
issues.next: Have the leak traced. If oil has reached the clutches, the seals and the clutch usually need replacing together.

issues.t: Doors won't latch or may open while driving (recall)
issues.sym: A door will not stay shut, bounces back open, the door-ajar light or alarm comes on, or a door looks closed but is not.
issues.why: A small spring tab inside the side door latches can break, especially in hot weather. Ford recalled these cars several times and later re-checked earlier latch repairs.
issues.next: Do not drive with a door that will not latch. Check your VIN for open door latch recalls; the latch replacement is free at a Ford dealer.

issues.t: Fuel pump can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine may stall without warning while driving or fail to restart.
issues.why: Some fuel pump parts were plated incorrectly and can fail. Ford recalled affected cars to replace the fuel pump.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for the fuel pump recall. A dealer replaces the pump free.

issues.t: Fuel tank may leak (recall)
issues.sym: A raw gasoline smell or fuel dripping under the car.
issues.why: A manufacturing error on some fuel tanks can let fuel leak, which is a fire risk. Ford recalled these cars for a new tank.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, park outside away from anything that could spark it and check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Right side curtain airbag may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: No warning to the driver. With the front passenger seat empty, the right-side curtain airbag may not fire in a side crash, leaving a rear passenger unprotected.
issues.why: The airbag software turned off the right curtain airbag whenever the front passenger seat was empty. Ford recalled the cars to reprogram it.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the free software update done if it is still open.

issues.t: Cylinder head can crack if coolant runs low (recall)
issues.sym: Overheating, oil leaking onto hot engine parts, smoke from under the hood, or in the worst case a fire.
issues.why: On the Fiesta ST engine, running with low coolant can overheat and crack the cylinder head. Ford recalled these cars to add a coolant level sensor and new software that warns the driver.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and keep an eye on the coolant level. Stop driving and turn the engine off if it overheats.

issues.t: Coolant loss and head gasket failure (ST)
issues.sym: The coolant level keeps dropping with no puddle, the engine runs hot, or there is white smoke from the exhaust.
issues.why: Coolant loss that ends in head gasket failure is one of the best-known Fiesta ST problems, more common on earlier cars. Ford later used an updated head gasket.
issues.next: Top up with the correct coolant and have a pressure test done soon. Fixing a small leak early can prevent a head gasket job.

issues.t: Coolant leak from thermostat housing or water pump
issues.sym: A sweet smell, drips or crusty residue on the passenger side of the engine, a dropping coolant level, or the temperature gauge rising.
issues.why: The plastic thermostat housing and the water pump on the 1.6L engine are common leak points as they age. The water pump is one of the most-replaced parts on these cars.
issues.next: Top up the coolant and have the leak found before the engine overheats. Running low on coolant can damage the head gasket.

issues.t: Coolant loss and white smoke (1.0L EcoBoost)
issues.sym: The coolant level drops, white smoke comes from the exhaust, and the engine may run rough.
issues.why: Ford's bulletin for this engine says that when no outside leak can be found, the exhaust manifold built into the cylinder head can crack and let coolant in.
issues.next: Stop topping up and driving on it for long. Have a shop do an extended cooling system pressure test and check the head for cracks.

issues.t: Turbo wastegate rattle (1.0L EcoBoost)
issues.sym: A metallic rattle from the turbo area, most noticeable at idle or when lifting off the gas.
issues.why: The rod that opens and closes the turbo's wastegate (the valve that limits boost) can wear and rattle. Ford issued a service message about it.
issues.next: It is mostly a noise, but have it checked so it is not confused with something more serious.

issues.t: Lack of power and misfire codes (1.0L EcoBoost)
issues.sym: The car feels weak, the check engine light comes on, and the engine may shake or misfire.
issues.why: Ford issued a service message for these engines about lack of power with misfire codes. Coolant getting into a cylinder can also cause misfires on this engine.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask the dealer about the related service messages before replacing parts.

issues.t: Low boost and lack of power (ST)
issues.sym: The ST feels flat, boost is low or comes and goes, and the check engine light may show boost codes.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin for lack of power with boost codes on this engine. The boost control solenoid is a common replacement part.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the boost control parts and hoses checked for leaks.

issues.t: Turbo wastegate rattle on cold start (ST)
issues.sym: A rattle from the turbo when the engine is cold, sometimes with a small loss of power.
issues.why: The wastegate linkage on the ST turbo can wear and rattle.
issues.next: Have the turbo linkage inspected. A worn actuator or linkage is usually the fix.

issues.t: Carbon buildup causes rough idle (ST)
issues.sym: Rough idle, slower throttle response and occasional misfires as mileage climbs.
issues.why: This engine sprays fuel straight into the cylinders, so fuel never washes the intake valves and carbon slowly builds up on them.
issues.next: If the engine runs rough, have a shop check for carbon buildup. Cleaning the valves (often by walnut-shell blasting) usually restores smooth running.

issues.t: Manual clutch slipping or hard to select gears (ST)
issues.sym: The engine revs rise without the car speeding up, the clutch pedal feels heavy, or it is hard to get into reverse, first or second.
issues.why: Hard driving wears the clutch, and worn synchronizers make some gears hard to engage.
issues.next: Have the clutch and gearbox checked. A slipping clutch only gets worse and can overheat the flywheel.

issues.t: Front brakes may drag and overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Brakes that feel like they are sticking, a hot or burning smell from the wheels, or the car pulling.
issues.why: Some front calipers were assembled with the wrong fluid, which made the seals swell and the brakes drag. Ford recalled the cars to flush the brake fluid and replace the front calipers and hoses.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. Dragging brakes can overheat and lose stopping power.

issues.t: Backup camera shows blank or distorted image (recall)
issues.sym: The rearview camera screen is blank, flickers or shows a distorted picture when in reverse.
issues.why: The camera can fail intermittently. Ford has recalled 2019 cars more than once to inspect and replace the camera.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open camera recalls and look over your shoulder when backing up until it is fixed.

issues.t: Blower fan only works on high
issues.sym: The heater and A/C fan works only on the highest setting, or not at all on lower settings.
issues.why: On cars with manual climate controls, the blower motor resistor behind the glove box fails. This is the most-reported problem RepairPal lists for these years.
issues.next: A shop or a handy owner can replace the resistor. Check that the blower motor connector is not melted at the same time.

issues.t: No heat on cold mornings from frozen blower motor
issues.sym: After a cold night the fan will not blow and you get little or no heat. The blower fuse may blow and the cabin filter may be wet.
issues.why: Snow gets past the cowl grille at the base of the windshield, melts into the heater box and freezes the blower motor overnight. Ford issued a bulletin for it.
issues.next: Ask a Ford dealer about bulletin 18-2024. The fix deals with the water path, and the blower motor and fuse may need replacing.

issues.t: Rough running or no start from ignition coil fault
issues.sym: The engine shakes, runs rough or will not start, with the check engine light on and ignition coil codes stored.
issues.why: Ford issued a service message for the 1.6L engine for ignition coil circuit codes with rough running or no start.
issues.next: Have the codes read. A dealer can check the coil, wiring and connector using Ford's service message.

issues.t: Hard start after refueling
issues.sym: The engine cranks a long time or stalls right after filling the tank, sometimes with a check engine light for the evaporative system.
issues.why: The canister purge valve can stick open and let fuel vapor flood the engine just after a fill-up.
issues.next: Have the evaporative codes read. Replacing the purge valve is usually a simple fix.

issues.t: Radio or SYNC freezes or stops working
issues.sym: The radio goes silent, the screen freezes, or Bluetooth will not connect.
issues.why: The audio module can fail, often blamed on heat and cold, and early SYNC software is known to freeze.
issues.next: Try disconnecting the battery for several minutes and check the radio fuses. Ask the dealer about SYNC software updates before buying a new unit.

issues.t: Clunking over bumps from worn shocks or struts
issues.sym: Knocking or clunking over bumps, a bouncy ride, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: Shock absorbers, struts and rear axle bushings are among the most-replaced parts on the Fiesta as the cars age.
issues.next: Have the suspension inspected. Replace shocks or struts in pairs.
